summary: Auth-config reads and updates must prove legacy-cache removal, reject redirects into the protected route, expose only explicitly audited scalar metadata, and keep credential inputs out of CLI arguments and MCP calls.
reason: Supabase AuthConfigResponse contains provider secrets, SMTP credentials, hook signing material, SMS credentials, and credential-capable Auth Hook URIs; filtering after serialization can leak those values to stdout, files, webhooks, MCP tools, or world-readable cache files.
validated_outcome: Synthetic credential sentinels are absent from all output and error paths; protected GET/PATCH operations fail closed unless legacy HTTP caches are removed and never cache responses; redirects into the protected route and credential-capable Auth Hook URIs are denied; secret-valued flags and the MCP update route fail closed with stdin guidance.
